up.note: Lemma 38, for every (possibly partial) Boolean $f$. The ingredient is Lemma 37 in its localised form: if $x$ and $y$ differ exactly on a block $B$ and the algorithm separates them, then the cost it spends inside $B$ is $\Omega(1)$. Fix an optimal noisy algorithm and let $p_i$ be the expected cost it spends on coordinate $i$; then $\sum_{i\in B} p_i = \Omega(1)$ for every sensitive block $B$, so $(p_i)$ is (a constant multiple of) a feasible solution to the fractional block sensitivity LP at $x$, and $\mathrm{fbs}(f) \le O(\sum_i p_i) = O(\mathrm{noisyR}(f))$.

up.note: The fractional refinement of $\mathrm{bs} \le \mathrm{Adv}^2$ [Ambainis02], by the same star matrix with the LP weights written onto its edges. Fix $x$ attaining $\mathrm{fbs}$, with weights $w_B$ on the sensitive blocks $B$ (so $\sum_{B i i} w_B \le 1$ for every $i$, and $\sum_B w_B = \mathrm{fbs}$). Put $\Gamma[x, x^B] = \Gamma[x^B, x] = \sqrt{w_B}$ and $0$ elsewhere. This is legal: each $x^B$ lies in $\mathrm{Dom}$ with $f(x^B) e f(x)$ by the definition of a sensitive block, and distinct blocks give distinct strings, so $\Gamma$ is a nonnegative matrix supported on pairs of unequal value. It is a weighted star, whose spectral norm is the $\ell_2$ norm of its edge weights: $\|\Gamma\| = \sqrt{\sum_B w_B} = \sqrt{\mathrm{fbs}}$. And $\Gamma \circ D_i$ keeps exactly the edges with $i \in B$, another star, so $\|\Gamma \circ D_i\| = \sqrt{\sum_{B i i} w_B} \le 1$. Hence $\mathrm{Adv}(f) \ge \sqrt{\mathrm{fbs}(f)}$. Nothing here uses totality -- the blocks were required to land in $\mathrm{Dom}$ from the start -- which is the whole point: the total-function route to the same conclusion goes through $\mathrm{fbs} = \Theta(\mathrm{CA})$ or through [KulkarniTal16], and both of those hypotheses are load-bearing. With $\mathrm{Adv} \le \mathrm{Adv}^{\pm} = \Theta(\mathrm{Q})$ [SpalekSzegedy06, Reichardt11] this gives $\mathrm{fbs} = O(\mathrm{Q}^2)$, and with $\mathrm{RC} = \Theta(\mathrm{fbs})$ the same for $\mathrm{RC}$, off the promise.

lo.note:
A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
